author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory at GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, shown by first name then last name. One page, no paging, no navigation entry.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html renders a page listing every specialty the clinic knows, each under its stored name
each specialty is listed with the veterinarians holding it, each veterinarian shown as first name then last name (for example Helen Leary)
a specialty no veterinarian holds is listed with no veterinarian beside it, rather than left out
a veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
every specialty renders on the single page: no paging controls and no page parameter
specialties, and the veterinarians under each, render in a stable order across requests
no navigation entry and no link from any other page leads to the specialty directory; the page carries the shared navigation like every page (REQ-SYS-001)
page wording comes from the message bundles in every supported language, per REQ-LANG-002
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)
a navigation entry or any link leading to the specialty directory - deliberate, a follow-up request may add one
paging, filtering, or searching the specialty directory
notes: Product owner closed elicitation for this slice; no consultation-request opened. Narrow readings taken where the request was silent, each recorded in the PRD's Open Questions: an unheld specialty is still listed; only order stability is required; stored specialty names render untranslated. The missing navigation entry is a stated product decision, not a defect - PRD edge case 4 of the specialty directory and the last Open Question record it. Non-Goals table unchanged, so no scope_overrides. Design owns the route, the read path for specialties (no specialty repository exists today), and the template name; file_targets are best-effort. Language bundles: the base bundle is listed, all supported locales need the new keys.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is the existing read-page pattern applied to a second noun in the vet package: a declarative Spring Data repository, a controller that binds nothing and selects a view, and a Thymeleaf template on the shared layout fragment. One adjustment is new: the page needs both every stored Specialty and the Veterinarians holding each, and the Vet-to-Specialty mapping is unidirectional, so the read side assembles two repository reads into one page-scoped read model. Specialty gets its own read-only repository (SpecialtyRepository), which does not breach the aggregate rule: Specialty is a shared lookup entity referenced by identity through the vet_specialties join table, the same standing PetType has with PetTypeRepository, not an internal of the Vet aggregate. The route lives in a new SpecialtyController rather than in VetController, following the owner package's one-controller-per-domain-noun precedent (OwnerController, PetController, VisitController) and the naming rule in architecture-principles.md (controller prefixed by the domain noun or the surface it serves). Grouping and ordering live in an immutable SpecialtyDirectory read model with a static factory, not in the controller: the Web controller row of the pattern catalog admits no rule, and system-design.md records the existing controller-logic deviation as not extending to new rules. The template is named for the ubiquitous-language term (specialtyDirectory), which also avoids the rejected alias 'specialty list'. primary_paths supersede the prd-entry's file_targets on the controller and template names, which that record marks best-effort and assigns to design. No docs/ edit accompanies this verdict: system-design.md carries current state, and the new contracts do not exist yet - doc-sync records them after implementation.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html served from the vet package; the mapping takes no request parameter at all, which is how 'no page parameter' is enforced rather than by ignoring one
SpecialtyRepository is a new read-only Spring Data interface over the existing specialties table; no schema change, no seed-data change, no new cache - CacheConfiguration is untouched

the holder side reuses VetRepository.findAll(), which is already @Cacheable("vets"); the directory inherits that cache's no-eviction property unchanged, since the application still has no vet write path (system-design.md Open Questions item 5)

the template replaces the shared layout fragment like every page (REQ-SYS-001) and passes a menu name matching no nav item, so navigation renders with nothing highlighted and fragments/layout.html is not edited - that is what keeps the no-nav-entry and no-inbound-link criterion true

new message keys land in all eleven bundles under src/main/resources/messages/ (REQ-LANG-002); I18nPropertiesSyncTest walks src/main HTML and fails on literal page text, so every visible string in the template comes from #{...}
docs follow-up for doc-sync after the slice lands: the Contracts table gains SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyController, and SpecialtyDirectory rows carrying Implements REQ-VET-003

patterns.description: name-ordered read of a shared lookup entity - the shape SpecialtyRepository copies. Prefer VetRepository's narrower base (extends Repository, not JpaRepository) with the single ordered finder: minimal surface, and nothing here needs write methods
route plus model attribute plus view-name return; the specialty route is the same shape minus the pagination helper
template head that replaces the layout fragment with an active-menu name; specialtyDirectory.html follows it with a menu name matching no nav item
getSpecialties() already sorts by name for display; it does not make the reverse grouping deterministic, which the read model must do itself

risks.risk: Grouping veterinarians under a Specialty by object identity silently yields empty holder lists. BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode, and the two reads run in separate persistence contexts (spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled, and the cached vet collection is detached), so a Specialty from SpecialtyRepository is never the same instance as the one inside Vet.getSpecialties().
risks.mitigation: Key the grouping on BaseEntity.getId(), not on object equality and not on name.

risks.risk: Arbitrary render order. Vet.specialties is a HashSet, and an unsorted findAll makes no order promise, so 'stable order across requests' fails by default.
risks.mitigation: Order specialties by name with the identifier as tie-break (nothing forbids two specialties sharing a name), and order the veterinarians under each by last name, then first name, then identifier. Sort in the read model, so a test can assert order without HTTP. Display stays first name then last name, independent of the sort key.

risks.risk: A supported language left partly translated. The bundle-parity check compares key sets, so an English string copied into all eleven files passes the test while breaching REQ-LANG-002's second clause.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing keys where the wording already fits (vets, specialties, none) and add only the keys the page genuinely needs, translated per locale rather than duplicated.

risks.risk: The empty cases render as a failure instead of an empty page. A clinic knowing no specialties and a specialty no veterinarian holds are both required to render.
risks.mitigation: The read model returns an empty entry list rather than null, and an entry with no holders is a normal entry; the template iterates without an emptiness branch. Edge case 1 says 'no veterinarian beside it' - render nothing beside it; reusing #{none} is available but is not what the criterion asks for.

notes: Narrow readings taken where the requirement is silent, all consistent with the prd-entry's own record: an unheld specialty is an ordinary entry with an empty holder list; stored specialty names render untranslated (they are data, not page wording); order is stable but its key is unspecified, so an explicit deterministic comparator is chosen and only stability is asserted; the missing nav entry is honored by adding nothing to fragments/layout.html. || Trust boundary review: the slice adds one HTTP entry point that accepts no user-supplied input - no path variable, no request parameter, no form. Nothing to validate at the boundary beyond the route itself. Output is Thymeleaf-escaped by default and the template does not use th:utext. The route is read-only, so there is no partial write to fail closed on. Absent authentication is the recorded project-wide posture (NG-1, system-design.md Security Context), not a new gap this slice opens. || Test shape, for the implementer: the five prd-entry test names carry over verbatim into SpecialtyControllerTests as a @WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class) driving MockMvc, the one sanctioned mock. Both repositories are small declarative interfaces - prefer hand-written stubs over @MockitoBean, per the project's minimal-mocking rule; VetControllerTests' Mockito usage is tolerated legacy, not the pattern to copy. Ordering and grouping are asserted directly against SpecialtyDirectory without Spring. || Basis for the covering claims: no IDE oracle is connected in this run, so resolution rests on greps and file reads rather than symbol lookup - the weaker basis. Confirmed by reading the files: no SpecialtyRepository or SpecialtyController exists under the vet package, templates/vets holds only vetList.html, BaseEntity declares no equals or hashCode, and PetTypeRepository is the lookup-repository precedent. || No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit had nothing to judge.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyController, and package placement mirror the existing per-noun controller/repository pattern (VetController, PetTypeRepository) precisely, including javadoc style and constructor-injection form

SpecialtyDirectory is a well-documented immutable read model: static factory, private constructor, explicit total-order comparators with id tie-breaks for both specialty name and holder last/first name, defensive via Stream.toList() so no mutable state escapes

Grouping algorithm (holdersBySpecialtyId) correctly joins Vet-held Specialty instances to stored Specialty instances by identifier only, matching the documented rationale (BaseEntity has no equals/hashCode, separate persistence contexts)

Template reuses the exact ${name + ' '} span-per-item idiom already established in vetList.html, and reuses existing translated message keys (specialties/name/vets) rather than adding English-only synonyms, per the design-block's decision
checkFormat, compileJava, and compileTestJava all pass clean; no format or compile issues introduced
Tests (read as context, not graded here) exercise ordering, tie-breaking, and empty-holder/no-specialty edge cases directly against the read model, keeping the controller test focused on HTTP wiring

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain not verified against the NVD in this review: the project configures no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin (build.gradle declares java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management, native, cyclonedx, javaformat), and this reviewer has no network access. The change introduces no dependency delta, so nothing here is newly unverified - but a human or CI should close the standing CVE check against the resolved Spring Boot 4.1.0 tree. A CycloneDX SBOM task is already available for that.

The directory reads the entire vet roster and the entire specialty table per request (SpecialtyController:128), where /vets.html paginates at 5. This matches the existing unpaged /vets JSON endpoint and the seeded data is tiny, so it is parity rather than a regression; if the roster ever grows, both unpaged readers should be revisited together.
approved_aspects: Output encoding: every dynamic value in src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyDirectory.html renders through th:text (entry.specialtyName, and each veterinarian name inside the th:each span). No th:utext, no th:attr/th:href carrying a model value, no inline script, no external resource reference, no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) of any model-derived value. The one preprocessing site in the codebase (fragments/layout.html:31) takes literal fragment arguments and is untouched by this change. Thymeleaf default escaping stays on, satisfying security-principles.md 'Cross-site scripting'.

No new attack surface at the request boundary: SpecialtyController.showSpecialtyDirectory takes only Model - no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @RequestBody, form binding, or @InitBinder. With nothing request-derived entering the handler, the mass-assignment, path-traversal, and injection rows of security-principles.md have no reachable instance here. The absent navigation entry was judged as the product decision it is, not as an access control; the endpoint is rated as public, and at that rating it exposes nothing new.

Data access: SpecialtyRepository is a Spring Data derived findAll() over the existing specialties table with no query text at all, so no string-concatenated query exists to attack. The interface extends the narrow Repository base (not JpaRepository) and declares one read method annotated @Transactional(readOnly = true) - least privilege at the persistence boundary, and no write path is opened. No schema, seed-data, or configuration change.

Data exposure parity: the page renders specialty names and vet full names, which the pre-existing /vets.html and the /vets JSON endpoint (VetController.showResourcesVetList, an unpaged findAll of the whole roster with specialties) already expose to the same anonymous caller. SpecialtyDirectory.Entry deliberately holds holder names as Strings rather than Vet entities, so no detached entity, identifier, or unrelated field reaches the view - the read model narrows the exposed surface relative to the vet list rather than widening it.

Concurrency and resource handling: SpecialtyController is a stateless singleton holding only final repository references; SpecialtyDirectory and its Entry are final classes with private constructors whose lists come from Stream.toList() (unmodifiable), and both comparators are stateless statics. No mutable shared state, no file handle, no stream, no executor, no SimpleDateFormat. The unpaged reads mirror the existing cached VetRepository.findAll() path and add no new unbounded allocation class.

No secrets, logging, or error-surface change: the diff adds no credential-shaped literal (swept for token/password/secret/key/credential/passwd/apikey across the change set), no logger call, no System.out/err, no exception construction, and no message that could carry internal detail outward. No deserialization, reflection, XML/YAML parsing, Runtime/ProcessBuilder, file I/O, or java.util.Random appears in the new code.
Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set and the diff adds no dependency, so the 'new dependency' checks in system-design.md are not triggered by this change.

author: test-reviewer
approved_aspects: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldGroupHoldersUnderTheSpecialtyTheyShareAnIdentifierWith is genuinely load-bearing: it constructs the stored Specialty and the vet-held Specialty as distinct instances sharing only an id, and neither BaseEntity, NamedEntity, nor Specialty overrides equals/hashCode (verified by reading all three), so a name- or equality-keyed grouping implementation would leave the holder list empty while the id-keyed SpecialtyDirectory.of implementation passes - the test discriminates the real defect class the design-block flagged

Order tests (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderSpecialtiesByName, ...SharingANameByIdentifier, ...OrderHoldersByLastNameThenFirstName) feed out-of-order/HashSet-backed input and assert an exact expected sequence via containsExactly, so they would catch a regression to HashMap/HashSet iteration order rather than passing incidentally on a lucky hash layout

All five prd-entry test_names carried over verbatim into SpecialtyControllerTests and each maps to a genuine PRD acceptance criterion or edge case (edge case 1 no-holder specialty, edge case 2 empty directory via the unit suite, edge case 3 stable order via the unit suite, single-page/no-paging via an explicit ?page=2 probe compared against the unpaged render)

Mocking policy honored: SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository are hand-written stubs (lambda and anonymous class), no new Mockito usage introduced; MockMvc is the one sanctioned mock for the controller test
100% line coverage on SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyController, and Specialty per jacocoTestReport, well above the docs/testing-principles.md 80% target

BDD naming (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}), four-phase structure without narration comments, AssertJ fluent chained assertions, role-named Tier-1 constants (RADIOLOGY_ID, HELEN_ID, etc.) with no mystery literals, and factory methods (createSpecialty/createVet) wrapping all construction - all consistent with docs/testing-principles.md

author: change-grader
summary: add the read-only specialty directory page

blast_radius.note: Nine files in one module, fifteen hunks, no sensitive paths, and zero deletions in production code: three new types and one new template that no existing class references, plus three doc files. The only touch on shared state is calling the pre-existing @Cacheable vets VetRepository.findAll, which is read-only and returns the same data /vets.html already serves, so no existing request path changes behavior.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks against the two risks the design flagged, both are actually handled rather than merely claimed: grouping keys on held.getId() through a HashMap (equals-based lookup, not reference identity), and both comparators are total with an id tie-break, so ordering is stable over Vet's HashSet and the unordered findAll. The trap I expected here does not fire either, since Vet.specialties is FetchType.EAGER, so the read model touching getSpecialties() outside the repository transaction cannot raise LazyInitializationException. The template mirrors vetList.html, escapes through th:text with no th:utext, and passes a layout menu argument matching no menuItem, which is exactly the deliberate no-nav-entry decision.

test_adequacy.note: The tests would fail against a broken implementation rather than restate it. SpecialtyDirectoryTests builds two distinct Specialty instances sharing an id, which fails outright under identity or equals-based grouping, and asserts the shared-name case that a non-total comparator would leave arbitrary. SpecialtyControllerTests renders the real Thymeleaf template through MockMvc against hand-written stubs and asserts on the returned HTML, with the VetRepository stub throwing on findAll(Pageable) to pin that the page never pages. The only mild brittleness is doesNotContain page= asserting against the whole rendered layout.

reviewer_hedging.note: Round two is unanimous approval, but the security reviewer parked two recommendations on that late-round approval rather than closing them: the doc row wording that reads as though Entry carried Vet objects (self-marked no change needed), and the supply-chain check, which was never verified against the NVD in round one for lack of network access and was explicitly not re-run in round two, carrying forward as recorded rather than verified. Round one also cost a full cycle on a doc-reviewer critical/blocked finding tagged bar_clause legible-cold, and its fix left a pre-existing Contracts preamble imprecision (public type against package-private controllers) open as a separate doc-sync item.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, zero consultations, zero build retries, and the diff maps one-to-one onto the requirement's five Done-when clauses and four edge cases with nothing beyond them. The second review cycle added Contracts table rows in response to a doc finding, which is a documentation gap closing rather than scope drift, and the three unresolved product questions are recorded in the PRD's Open Questions rather than silently decided in code.

rationale: Additive, contained, and the two load-bearing risks the design named are genuinely handled in the code, not just asserted. What deserves a look is not the diff but the residue around it: the supply-chain CVE check was never run for this slice in either round, and the Contracts preamble imprecision stays open. Confirm both are acceptable to carry, then merge.
